headline: Precision medicine through AI-informed clinical decision support.
researchQuestionLead: The core question that we are addressing
researchQuestion: How can Agentic AI support interdisciplinary research teams in overcoming the barriers to navigating and creating advanced modeling workflows for Precision Medicine?
overview: The potential to learn from the wealth of real-world health data holds great promise, including the highly desirable large-scale shift towards Precision Medicine through AI-informed clinical decision support.

Clinical teams can now make increasingly complex treatment decisions using multiple data types, ranging from quantitative features to images and text. However, in practice, optimally modeling multimodal, heterogeneous and longitudinal data sources in a meaningful way for specialized disease prediction is challenging and cannot always be achieved with a one-size-fits-all approach that generalist foundation models provide.
In fact, tackling grand challenges in Precision Medicine with the development of specialized AI-based decision support systems requires a close synergy among interdisciplinary research teams.

premises.title: Fundamental premises
premises.scope:
favoring clinical translation
of computer science methods
items: Specialized predictive models in medicine need to be packaged as reusable agents
Agentic AI also needs to be deployed locally in hospital settings to preserve data confidentiality
Software engineering is required to enhance the working synergy of interdisciplinary teams

longTermVision: Guided by these premises, the long-term vision of our research is to support clinical decisions towards improved Precision Medicine by bridging Generalist/Specialist/Precision Medical AI within an integrated Agentic AI system. Currently, our research focuses on Specialist Medical AI.

approach.lead: For this purpose, we anchor our work on
approach.description: an open-source platform developed by our group.

progressMilestone: Version 1.0 of the MEDomics platform was launched in 2024.
integration: As described below, the contributions at MEDomicsLab span three main research axes (I, II, III), with the development of the MEDomics platform acting as a cross-cutting axis dedicated to the integration of all methodological developments into a common working environment.
scopeTitle: Clinically Grounded AI Tools for Better Precision Medicine

axes.title: Medical data modeling & deployment
paragraphs: We developed graph neural network methods to disentangle interactions in multimodal healthcare data [JA1] and to correct model predictions after training [CP1, CP2].

Our Ensemble Longitudinal Network (ELN) helped us assess what past patient records contribute to one-year mortality risk predictions in a private dataset in Sherbrooke, Québec [JA2]. We released an associated synthetic dataset of 123,646 patients for other researchers to investigate this question [CP3].
For safer deployment, MED3pa identifies patient profiles for which a given binary classifier makes low-confidence predictions [JA3] and helps explain the sources of that uncertainty [CP4].

axes.title: Medical image analysis
paragraphs: We used transformers to encode whole-slide histopathology images and developed an image-centered multimodal fusion framework for predicting outcomes across several cancers [JA4]. In high-grade prostate cancer, our multi-task Sequential Network (SN) refines predictions as earlier outcomes become available and influence treatment management [JA5, CP5].
In radiomics, we optimized renal mass histology prediction [JA6] and contributed to international reference standards for computing convolutional filters in medical images [JA7].

axes.title: Open-source software engineering
paragraphs: MEDomics is the core component of our research program. It helps clinical researchers and computer scientists work together on medical data modeling. Its interactive front end generates code that links to a reproducible back-end package. The platform runs on standard research laptops.

Seven modules span three layers. Design contains Input, Extraction and Exploratory. Development contains Machine Learning, Evaluation and Federated Learning. Deployment contains Application. Standalone applications extend this work through MED3pa, MEDiml [JA8] and MEDfl.

ecosystem.title: MEDomics platform
lead: Today, it is also powered by the standalone sub-applications MED3pa, MEDiml and MEDfl.

apps.name: MEDomics
apps.caption: And more is coming.
apps.alt: MEDomics card: “Many inputs. One workflow.” Images, tables and time series converge into one design, development and deployment workflow.

apps.name: MED3pa
apps.alt: MED3pa card: “Look closer at model confidence.” A grid of patient profiles flags those with lower prediction confidence.

apps.name: MEDiml
apps.alt: MEDiml card: “From pixels to features.” CT, MRI and PET images become reproducible radiomic features.

apps.name: MEDfl
apps.alt: MEDfl card: “Learn together.” Four institutions train a shared model while their data stays local.

gaps: Despite significant development progress, the MEDomics platform currently consists of static modules, and interdisciplinary research teams still face a steep learning curve to master the utilities of each module and their interconnection. Furthermore, the platform lacks methodological tools to efficiently account for patient care trajectories in multimodal modeling setups, which limits its utility in addressing real-world Precision Medicine scenarios.
work: In the next years, our goal is to reengineer MEDomics into a platform assisted by local Agentic AI, to optimize collaboration among interdisciplinary teams in advanced medical data modeling research

program.title: Vision of our research program.
program.caption: Our current program (solid lines) currently focuses on Specialist Medical AI for Precision Medicine, within the long-term vision (dashed lines) of Agentic AI bridging Generalist/Specialist/Precision Medical AI.
